abstract: Bulk transcriptomes carry information on diagnosis, treatment response and survival, but clinical cohorts are small, and each gets a model of its own that often fails in the next cohort. Here we present PRTS, a 220-million-parameter model that reads a labelled cohort as context and predicts binary, multiclass, continuous or survival endpoints for new samples from whole transcriptomes, without per-cohort training. PRTS was pretrained on 6.0 million tasks generated from public RNA-seq profiles. On 175 held-out tasks and 44 tasks from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), it had the highest mean predictive accuracy, narrowly ahead of TabPFN v3.5, the strongest pre-specified comparator. The lead came from within-cohort prediction and, on TCGA, mainly from survival tasks; across cohorts and at unseen sites, PRTS was level with the strongest tabular models while running more than twice as fast as TabPFN v3.5. The same weights transfer labels to new cohorts from public references, forecast accuracy from pilots, flag suspect labels and attribute predictions to genes. We release the prior, the pretraining code and the model with its weights, together with RealBulk, a collection of 1,160 curated public cohorts, and its benchmark.
